Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an AI agent pane: a React/TypeScript page under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/` and the host under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Read `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`, and the tool error contract (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`, one code list shared by in-app and MCP tools) first. The agent's standing instructions live in the page (`projectInstructions.ts` and the skills under `AgentUI/src/skills/`), with `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guarding the text the model reads. Kenneth's prompt rules: the standing prompt holds principles only, situational text comes from state channels and skills; no live-model prompt evals without Kenneth approving a specific batch, because they cost money. On 2026-10-28 a UX walkthrough of the built app (jusprin-newui, Claude Opus 5.5) found two trust problems in the chat; critique with screenshots at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR, frames 2A-03, 1A-03 and 2A-03 again. Kenneth wants the session to discuss the optimal user experience with him before implementing anything: bring him the choices, then stop. Rules: temp docs untracked, never committed; web bundle rebuilt through CMake; guard tests shown to fail first; do not commit unless Kenneth asks; check `pgrep -fl ninja` and build with `-j4`. Reproduction routes: the real app (scratch copies of the built .app and of `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2`, `local_machines` set to `{}`, `--datadir <scratch>`, open `~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf`, slice, click the "1 print issue" chip, press Ask AI; the web view needs full-screen computer control, approved by Kenneth per request), or the page fixture route with a fake `window.wx` host for page-only states.

Task:
Two problems in the chat pane, both about whether the person can trust what it says.

Problem 1: the activity row under an answer reads "Worked for 4s · 1 action · 1 failed" with no sentence about what failed. The answer above it was fine, but a careful person distrusts an answer that admits a failure it will not explain. The app log carried no line for the failure either. Frame 2A-03 of the critique shows the row. Find which tool call failed in that turn (it followed the Ask AI button on the heatbed warning), why the row shows a count instead of the error, and whether the failed call's error code and message are available to the page at all.

Problem 2: the agent claims actions it did not take. In 1A-03 it wrote "When I opened the file, I switched the filament setting from PLA Matte to PLA Basic to match the file" when the file's embedded settings did that; in 2A-03 it wrote "I show this warning for every PLA print" when OrcaSlicer raised the warning. Find what the model is told about file-load changes (the load report's `selectedSetupChange` and the `file-loaded` skill) and about slice warnings (`sliceWarnings`, the `print-issues` skill) that leads it to speak in the first person about them, and what the instructions already say about attribution.

Task, in this order:
1. Reproduce both in the real app or from the saved project record of the walkthrough, and trace the causes as above.
2. Write an untracked note (`chat-trust-options.md` in the worktree root) for Kenneth, and discuss it with him before any code: for problem 1, two or three ways the row can state the failure (an expandable line with the tool's name and its error message in the person's words; the agent being made to mention it in the reply; both), with where each lives (page, host, prompt) and what happens for an MCP client; for problem 2, the wording change in the instructions or skills that makes attribution honest, how a guard test in `wording.test.ts` would hold it, and what evidence short of a live-model batch would show the change works, since live runs need Kenneth's approval of a specific batch.
3. Stop and wait for Kenneth's decisions. Do not implement before he answers.

Done, after his choice, means: the activity row states what failed in plain words, covered by a Vitest test; the instruction wording changed with a guard test that was shown to fail first; a replay of the two walkthrough turns through the request recorder or a stub model shows the new wording in the request; verified in the real app with a screenshot of a failed-action row if Kenneth approves screen control; nothing committed until he says so; report what was verified and what was not.

# The first message after a file is opened or imported

The rules above still apply. For this one response, write the first message about the file just opened or imported, by the person or by a tool call of mine. Report and offer from the report and the picture, and change nothing the person has not asked for.

The report separates four sources. The app-computed opening outcome (loadFacts, loads, and objects) establishes what was loaded and how the selected printer, material and print settings changed. A load's withSettings only says the app requested settings, not that it applied them; claim they were applied only when loadFacts.settingsOutcome says applied. If that outcome is absent, leave the application of settings uncertain. The current workspace establishes what is selected now; setupPrinters lists printer models the person has set up in JusPrin, each with bedMm, its bed's width, depth and printable height; selectedPrinterBedMm is the selected printer's. For each object, placedOnBed says whether it sits wholly on the bed now, clear of any area the printer's profile excludes, and fitsSelectedBed and fitsSetupPrinters whether its size fits each bed somewhere, turned a quarter-turn if needed: an object that is off the bed but fits it needs moving, not resizing. mesh is the app's check of the model: shells is how many separate pieces it is made of, openEdges or repairedErrors above zero mean holes or errors in it, and unitsSuspicion says when its size looks like inches or metres. customized lists what the file already prepared for printing: painted supports, seams, colours or fuzzy skin, and its own layer heights. fileFacts is what each 3MF says about itself: the app that saved it, the printer and nozzle it was made for, and its filaments. Neither a selection nor that list proves which physical machine they intend to use. The raw messages.items contain Orca's dialog title and text, offered buttons, and the answer JusPrin supplied automatically. The person did not choose that answer and may never have seen the dialog. The file's details.description and details.profileDescription are author notes: claims from the file, not proof that their advice was applied. The picture, when present, is the active plate after the load, rendered from the iso view.

Look at the attached picture when there is one. Check the selected printer, filament and process presets and the plate type against the file and against the printers the person has set up; when one looks wrong for this print, say which and suggest the one to use, without changing it. When an object does not fit the selected printer, name a set-up printer it fits, from fitsSetupPrinters.

Write about 80 words, with at most two bullets, about what matters for this file now. The person sees the setup card above your message, with the presets, the plate and the estimates, and the activity line under your turn, with the checks you made: leave those to them rather than restating them.
- Lead with what decides whether or how it can print: a load that failed, an object that does not fit, a printer to choose, settings or G-code that need review. Say it once, with only the numbers that matter.
- Say what you take the object to be, and how it should be printed, only when that changes the advice, and then briefly, as a guess. Leave other advice (material, strength, orientation) until the main decision is made.
- Do not explain routine loading: how the file was opened, whether its settings were applied, or which notices appeared, unless it changes the next step. Do not imply that loading the file ran G-code on a printer. Never claim a warning was fixed merely because its dialog was dismissed.
- When nothing needs attention, say so in a sentence.
- End with exactly one question, about the next step: the message's only question, not a menu of alternatives. Do not offer to print while the intended printer or another consequential choice is unresolved.

Read each actual notice with its automatic answer and the final opening outcome. The guide below is deliberately not a code classification table.

| Notice or event you may encounter | Importance and explanation for the person |
| --- | --- |
| A newer or partly incompatible 3MF asks whether to continue | If opening succeeded, mention a lost or changed feature only when the outcome shows one. If it failed, explain the failure. Omit a version warning with no consequence. |
| Settings were substituted with supported values | Usually omit when completed successfully. Explain briefly if the result materially changes the print or still needs a choice. |
| “Customized Preset” or a file setting has no installed match | This alone does not establish that machine commands changed. Use the final selected printer and material to judge the consequence. |
| “Modified G-code” | When the notice says so, the file includes modified G-code in its printer or filament settings, and I warned about it while opening the file. G-code is the instructions a printer runs. Name the affected setting if the notice gives it and that helps locate what to review; do not invent a line number or claim I inspected the commands. Explain that these instructions need review before printing, without claiming they are safe or unsafe. Offer to review the modified G-code next. |
| Invalid values in a 3MF | If the model loaded, say which file settings need checking when their names are supplied. Do not say they were corrected unless the outcome establishes that. |
| Zero-volume parts were removed | Mention omitted parts when they could change the intended model. If nothing usable remains, lead with the failed opening. |
| “Object too small” asks whether to scale | The recorded answer says whether JusPrin scaled it. If it stayed tiny, state its final numeric size and ask the intended size. If scaled, mention the conversion only if it matters. |
| “Object too large” asks whether to shrink | The answer and final dimensions say whether it was shrunk. If still too large, explain the bed-fit problem. If shrunk, explain that its intended size may have changed. |
| A choice to open a 3MF as a project or geometry only | Use loadFacts.settingsOutcome to say whether the file's print settings were applied. Explain only when it changes the next step. |
| Connected-printer synchronization | Use the final selection and separately supplied connection state. Do not infer a connected machine from a preset name. |
| OBJ colour mapping, STEP mesh options, or unreadable STEP names | Mention a resulting colour, shape, precision or naming problem only when it matters to this model. |
| Multiple parts or files become one object | Mention grouping only if it changes how the person can print or edit the model. |
| A suggestion to simplify a very detailed model | Usually omit from the first message unless a current performance or editing problem exists. |
| A refusal to mix G-code with models, open multiple G-code files, or add models in preview mode | If the requested file did not open, explain that directly and give the next useful step. |
| “File contains no geometry” or a loading error | Lead with what failed and what, if anything, was added. Give the actual reason when available; do not invent one. |

An alarming notice does not override the final outcome. An automatic “No”, “Yes” or “OK” is JusPrin's action, not the person's preference. If selectedSetupChange.printerPreset exists, name both its from and to selections in plain language, then ask which printer the person intends to use. Do not turn an already completed change into a fresh action item.

Use useful file author advice only when it affects the next step; keep it secondary to an unresolved printer or size decision. Attribute it to the file.

When the workspace's plan needs reassessment (its validity is needs_reassessment because the person imported this file into a project that already had a plan), record the plan again with setup_record in this reply: a new headline if the file changes how you will print, the same headline if the plan still holds. That clears the mark on the setup card; nothing else does.

Write in uiLanguage when it is supplied. Keep it short.

# Issues I report about the print

The rules above still apply. This request is the first to carry something I reported about the print: the person pressed a button on a print-issue chip (their message has a <print_issue> block), or a slice finished with warnings that plate's last slice did not have (the plate's sliceWarnings, in the workspace and in a tool result's slicing section; slice_report's findings section has the full list, except the heatbed warning and a repeated timelapse one).

How to read a finding. A blocker means I will not slice or print until it is fixed; a warning means the slice exists and can print; a critical warning is one I flag as serious. The setting key names what to change, and settings_search or settings_get with that key tells what the setting is and its value now. Untracked working note, 2026-10-28. Branch `claude/chat-trust` (= jusprin-newui 2d3fc8157a, no changes yet). Nothing is implemented; four questions for you are at the end.

Evidence comes from the walkthrough's saved project record (`p-a64e4967dc221bab-…/current-state.json` in the walkthrough session's scratch data folder) and from a no-model reproduction: I started a scratch copy of the walkthrough's built app on a copy of its data folder (`local_machines` emptied) and called the tools over the app's MCP server. Every model message quoted below comes from that saved record.

## Problem 1: "Worked for 4s · 1 action · 1 failed"

### What failed

After Ask AI on the heatbed warning, the model made one call:

```
settings_get  scope: filament, target.preset: "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1M"
              keys: textured_plate_temp, textured_plate_temp_initial_layer, temperature_vitrification
→ unknown_preset: No filament preset is named "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1M".
  suggestions: ["Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1M"]
```

The error contradicts itself: the name it rejects is the selected filament, and it suggests that same name. The setup card above the chat also says Bambu PLA Basic.

**The cause is a host bug, and I reproduced it.** `scope_preset()` (Workspace/OrcaSettings.hpp:251) only accepts a preset that has `is_visible` set. The 3MF selected "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1M", but that preset is not in the person's visible filament list. The app config's `filaments` list has the A1 variant and "PLA Matte @BBL A1M", not "PLA Basic @BBL A1M". So the filament Orca is printing with cannot be read by name. In the reproduction, the same call failed exactly as above. With "Bambu PLA Matte @BBL A1M" it worked and returned bed 65 °C and softening point 45 °C.

**The failure changed the answer.** The model had no numbers to work from, so it wrote "PLA starts to soften at about 55–60 °C" and "the bed is set at or near that softening temperature". The person's own preset says 45 °C. The reply gives no sign that these figures are general knowledge and not the person's settings.

### Why the row shows only a count

`turnLineText()` in `AgentUI/src/components/TurnActivity.tsx` builds the closed line as duration · count · "N failed". Clicking the line opens one row per action. That row already shows the error, as `actionLineText()` renders it: `Read settings · No filament preset is named "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1M".` So the information exists, but it is hidden behind a click. The text is also written for the model (the tool error contract makes the message say what to do next), and in this case it reads as nonsense to a person.

### Is the error available to the page?

Yes, in full. The page state stores `error.code`, `error.message` and `error.details` on the activity, and `actionLineText()` already reads the message. Nothing new is needed from the host for the row.

### The missing log line

`ToolExecutionCoordinator::fail()` (Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:2336) records the error and notifies observers, but logs nothing. In the reproduction, the app's debug log (13,746 lines) has no line for the failure.

### MCP clients

Calls from an MCP client (source `mcp`) are not tied to any chat turn, so no activity row ever shows them. The client gets `isError: true` with the code and message, and the server instructions already say "refused or failed, stop and tell the person". A change to the row therefore does nothing for MCP. A change to the in-app standing prompt does not reach an MCP client's model either. The host bug fix and the log line do apply to MCP.

### Options

**1A. The row says it (page only).** The closed line names the failed action, for example `Worked for 4s · 1 action · Read settings didn't work`. The open row puts the reason in the person's words. That sentence comes from a page-side table with one entry per group of codes in ToolErrors.hpp, plus "Nothing was changed.", because the contract says a failed call changes nothing unless its message says otherwise. The host's own message moves into the row's tooltip for developers. A call that failed and then succeeded on a retry in the same turn would not count as failed. Cost: about one component, a code-to-words table, and a Vitest test. Limit: the row can say what failed, but not what the failure did to the answer, such as the guessed 55–60 °C.

**1B. The agent says it (prompt).** One principle in the standing prompt's Replies section, next to "After a tool result, say what actually happened in their terms": when a call failed and you answered without what it would have told you, say so in a sentence and say what the answer rests on instead. This is a standing principle, not situational text, so it fits your rule for the standing prompt. The guard is a string pin in `projectInstructions.test.ts`. Limit: it depends on the model, and the row still says "1 failed" with no reason.

**1C. Both (my recommendation).** The row is reliable and covers every failure. The reply covers the part only the model knows, which is how the failure changed the answer.

On top of any of these, I would do two small host fixes:
- Let `settings_get` read the selected filament or printer preset even when it is hidden. That removes this particular failure.
- Log one line in `fail()`, with the tool, code and message.

## Problem 2: the agent claims the app's actions

### Where the first person comes from

The prompt tells the model to do this:

- `projectInstructions.ts`, Role: "You are JusPrin, a 3D printing app … App messages and tool results may say OrcaSlicer; that is this app, so its warnings and actions are yours."
- `projectInstructions.ts`, Replies: "Speak in first person about the app's actions ("I sliced", never "OrcaSlicer warned")." This has been in place since 832bb47c31 (2026-10-01), and `skills.test.ts` pins the print-issues skill as "speaks as the app".
- The print-issues skill speaks as the app throughout: "Issues I report about the print", "A blocker means I will not slice", "A warning is my statement about the slice", "What I report while slicing", "I substitute a pattern", "I raise no slicing warning …".
- The file-loaded skill: "opened or imported, by the person or by a tool call of mine", and "Modified G-code … I warned about it while opening the file".

Given those lines, "I show this warning for every PLA print" is exactly what the model was told to write.

### Why the file-loaded sentence is also wrong on the facts

The report had `startedBy: "user"`, so the person opened the file, not the agent. It also had `selectedSetupChange.filamentPreset` Matte → Basic with `settingsOutcome: "applied"`, which means the file's settings made the switch. The skill mentions neither `startedBy` nor where a filament change comes from; it only covers a printer change.

### What the instructions already get right

"An automatic 'No', 'Yes' or 'OK' is JusPrin's action, not the person's preference." "Do not turn an already completed change into a fresh action item." "Attribute it to the file" (for the author's advice). The prompt separates the person from the app, but it never separates the agent's own choices from what the app does by rule.

### Options

**2A. Keep "I am the app", but claim only what you did (my recommendation).** The Role line loses "its warnings and actions are yours". The Replies rule becomes: speak as the app, in the first person, for what you did in this conversation. For what happened without you, name the cause instead of claiming a choice. That covers the file's settings applied on opening, a warning slicing raises by a fixed rule, and a dialog the app answered by itself. "Never 'OrcaSlicer warned'" stays. The skills carry the specifics:
- file-loaded: who opened the file comes from `startedBy`. A `selectedSetupChange` with `settingsOutcome: applied` came from the file's settings, so say "the file's settings switched the filament to PLA Basic". The Modified G-code row says "the app warned".
- print-issues: "I report / I substitute / my statement / I raise" become "slicing reports / the slicer substitutes / a warning is the slicer's statement / slicing raises no warning for …".

The new wording would read like this: "Opening the file switched the filament to PLA Basic, the one it was made for", and "This warning comes up for every PLA print".

**2B. The agent is an assistant inside JusPrin.** The model refers to the app in the third person ("JusPrin warns…", "JusPrin applied the file's filament"). This is a clearer model of who does what for the person, but it reverses your 2026-10-01 choice, rewrites every skill's voice, and flips the "speaks as the app" test.

**2C. Minimal.** Fix only the two file-loaded sentences and add the `startedBy` and `settingsOutcome` facts. This fixes 1A-03 but not 2A-03, because the Role line still says the app's warnings are the agent's.

### Guard test (any option)

A new case in `wording.test.ts` runs over every model-facing text: the skills, the instructions, the ToolRegistry literals and project_tools.json. It fails on the phrases that hand the app's automatic acts to the agent: `/\bI (warned|report|reported|raise|substitute|flag|will not slice)\b/`, "of mine", "my statement", and "its warnings and actions are yours". Run today, it fails on 8 lines across the two skills and the Role line. I will show that failing run before editing the text. A positive pin in `projectInstructions.test.ts` holds the new Replies sentence. Honestly, a phrase list guards against the known patterns coming back, not against new phrasings.

### Evidence without a live model

- **Request recorder.** Re-record the two walkthrough turns (the cable-holder 3MF opening, then Ask AI on the heatbed issue) with scripted model outputs. Then diff the recorded requests, normalised as before, against today's. This shows the old sentences are gone and the new ones reach the model. It proves the change is delivered, not that the model behaves differently.
- **Line-by-line trace.** Each of the two bad sentences traces to a specific instruction line quoted above. After the change, the guard test proves no line says the opposite. That is an argument, not a measurement.
- **The behaviour itself needs a model.** The smallest useful batch: resend the two recorded requests to Opus 5.5, 5 samples each, before and after. The heatbed turn includes the failed `settings_get` result, so it takes 2 requests per sample. That is about 30 requests. My estimate, not yet measured: about 25k input tokens each, mostly cached, so about 750k input and 15k output. I would count first-person claims of the filament switch and the warning, plus whether the reply mentions the failed read. I would only run this with your approval of that exact batch.

## Coordination

The issue-chip session (worktree `quirky-galileo-e428a3`, branch `claude/issue-chip-options`, commit 434e893a6b, unmerged) removes the heatbed row from the print-issues skill. It also drops the bed-temperature warning from the chip and slice_report. Once that merges, the 2A walkthrough (Ask AI on the heatbed chip) cannot happen any more, though the attribution problem still applies to every other warning. My print-issues edits should go on top of that branch, or after it merges, to avoid a conflict in the same file.

## Questions for you

1. **How should the row explain a failed action?** 1A puts it in the row only: the failed action's name, a reason in the person's words, and the host message in the tooltip. 1B has the agent mention it in the reply. 1C does both. I recommend 1C, because only the reply can say the 55–60 °C was a guess.
2. **Should I fix the two host problems in this change?** The first is that `settings_get` cannot read the selected preset when it is hidden. The second is that a failed call writes no log line. Both are small, both also help MCP clients, and both need the C++ build (`-j4`). I recommend yes.
3. **Which voice should the agent use?** 2A keeps "I am the app" but claims only what the agent did and names the cause of everything else. 2B makes the agent an assistant that calls the app "JusPrin" in the third person. 2C fixes only the file-opening sentence. I recommend 2A.
4. **Do you approve the live check?** It is about 30 Opus 5.5 requests (2 turns × 5 samples × before/after, plus the tool round-trip), roughly 750k input tokens, mostly cached. Without it, the evidence stops at "the new wording reaches the model".

content.text:
I traced both chat trust problems and reproduced the failed call without a model. My options note is [chat-trust-options.md](chat-trust-options.md); it is untracked, and nothing is changed or committed. I'm stopping here until Kenneth decides.

**Problem 1: "1 action · 1 failed"**
- **What failed:** after Ask AI, the agent called `settings_get` for the selected filament "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1M". The call failed with `unknown_preset` ("No filament preset is named …"), and the error then suggested that exact name.
- **Why it failed:** this is a host bug. `scope_preset()` in `Workspace/OrcaSettings.hpp` only accepts presets on the person's visible filament list. The 3MF picked one that isn't on it.
- **Reproduced:** I started a scratch copy of the walkthrough's app and called the tool over its MCP server. The call fails for the selected filament. For a filament on the visible list it works and returns bed 65 °C and softening point 45 °C.
- **It changed the answer:** without those numbers, the agent wrote "PLA starts to soften at about 55–60 °C" as if that were the person's setting.
- **The page already has the error:** it stores the error code and message. Clicking the row opens a line that shows the raw message, but that message was written for the model and reads as nonsense to a person.
- **No log line:** `ToolExecutionCoordinator::fail()` writes nothing to the app log.
- **MCP clients:** their calls never appear in a chat row. They already get the error code and message from the tool result.

**Problem 2: the agent claiming the app's actions**
- **The prompt asks for it.** The standing prompt says the app's "warnings and actions are yours" and "Speak in first person about the app's actions". The print-issues skill speaks as the app throughout ("I report", "I raise"), and the file-loaded skill says "I warned about it while opening the file".
- **The file-opening sentence is also wrong on the facts.** The load report said the person opened the file and that the file's settings made the filament switch. The skill doesn't tell the model to use either fact.

**Questions for Kenneth (written out in full at the end of the note):**
1. **How should a failure be explained?** I recommend both: the row names the failed action with a reason in plain words, and the agent says in its reply what the failure means for the answer. Only the reply can say the 55–60 °C was a guess.
2. **Should this change include two small host fixes?** One makes `settings_get` read the selected preset even when it's hidden; the other logs failed calls. Both need the C++ build. I recommend yes.
3. **Which voice should the agent use?** I recommend it keeps speaking as the app but claims only what it did in the chat, and names the cause of everything else ("the file's settings switched the filament", "this warning comes up for every PLA print"). A new test in `wording.test.ts` would catch the 10 lines that currently say otherwise.
4. **Do you approve a live check?** It would be about 30 Opus 5.5 requests (roughly 750k input tokens, mostly cached). Without it, the evidence only shows that the new wording reaches the model, not that its replies change.

One conflict to plan around: the issue-chip session's branch `claude/issue-chip-options` (434e893a6b, not merged) also edits the print-issues skill and removes the bed-temperature warning. My edits to that skill should go on top of it.
Discuss first

Here's how I see the two decisions that matter most. Push back on any of it.

**1. Which voice the agent uses (problem 2)**

This is the biggest decision, because it was a deliberate choice of yours on 2026-10-01. You told the model "You are JusPrin… its warnings and actions are yours", so the person sees one character instead of an agent plus a slicer. Under that rule, "I show this warning for every PLA print" is not really a lie: the app does show it for every PLA print. What the person loses is the difference between a choice and a rule. When the agent says "I switched the filament to PLA Basic", the person thinks it judged that PLA Basic was right. In fact the file's settings switched it, and nobody chose anything.

So I think the real question is whether the person needs to tell "the agent decided this" apart from "this happened automatically". I think they do, mainly for undo and blame. If the agent decided something, the person can argue with it. If the file decided, they need to know the file carries settings. Keeping the app voice but naming the cause ("opening the file switched the filament to the one it was made for") keeps your one-character design and fixes that. Making the agent a separate assistant that calls the app "JusPrin" is cleaner, but it means rewriting the voice of every skill. I don't think the problem justifies that.

One fact error stands apart from the voice question. "When I opened the file" is wrong in either voice, because the person opened it. The load report said so (`startedBy: user`), but no instruction tells the model to use it.

**2. Whether the agent must mention a failed call in its reply (problem 1)**

The row fix is easy and doesn't depend on the model. What I'd like your view on is whether failures also belong in the reply. The case for it: the failed read made the answer worse. The model filled in "about 55–60 °C" from general knowledge, and the person's preset says 45 °C. The row can't tell the person that a number in the answer is a guess, but the reply can. The case against: most failed calls are self-corrected (a wrong key, then a retry that works). A rule to mention failures could fill replies with "I couldn't read X at first". So I'd word it narrowly: mention it only when the answer had to go without what the call would have told you. A failure that a later call made up for stays out of the reply, and I'd keep it out of the row's "failed" count too.

**Two smaller questions**

- **The host bug that caused this failure.** The agent can't read settings of a selected preset when that preset isn't on the person's visible list. That will happen whenever a 3MF picks a preset the person never added. I think it should be fixed whatever we choose for the row, but it's C++ and can be a separate change if you'd rather keep this one to wording.
- **The row's wording for the person.** The error messages are written for the model, and some of them are nonsense to a person, like this one. I'd write one plain sentence per group of error codes, plus "Nothing was changed". The original message would go in a hover tooltip, so the detail isn't lost.

Which part do you want to settle first? I'd start with the voice question, since it decides how the skill edits read.

ignore the 2nd problem. For the first one, let's just add some debuggability for the failure. Check how other popular hard apps are currently showing debugging info. I'm under the impression that they are doing this using collapsible accordion. But check to make sure yourself. I think we can do something similar.

**Anatomy**

- **Tool icon** (optional): identifies the tool or function.
- **Tool label**: the tool or function name.
- **Separator** (optional).
- **Secondary label** (optional): extra context, such as a target, resource, or execution duration.
- **Status badge** (conditional): shows completed, awaiting-approval, or error status.
- **Expand/collapse control**: shows whether the content is visible.
- **Content container**: groups the details for the invocation.
- **Tool parameters** (optional): the data sent to the tool.
- **Tool result** (optional): the output from a completed call.

**States**

- **Active**: the invocation is in progress. No status badge appears, per the statement that "The active state does not display a status badge."
- **Completed**: the invocation finished successfully. A completed badge appears, and the result can show in the expanded content.
- **Awaiting approval**: the action needs user confirmation. The expanded content can include an approval message with Approve and Reject actions.
- **Error**: the invocation failed. An error badge appears, and the expanded content can show an error message.

**Header contents**

The header identifies the tool and includes the tool icon (optional), tool label, secondary label (optional), status badge (except in the active state), and expand/collapse control.

**Expanded content on error**

The expanded content container can present an error message. The source says this is optional ("can"), so it is not guaranteed. Parameters may also appear there, since they are optional display elements.

**Not covered in the source**

- Default expanded or collapsed behavior. The page does not say whether the component starts expanded or collapsed in any state, including error.
- Guidance on error message wording. The page does not provide copy guidelines or example messages.

For these details, check the framework-specific Tool Call documentation linked on the page.

result.output:
**Collapsed header:** Each tool call shows as a one-line button with a status icon (spinner, check, X-circle, or alert), a label, and an elapsed duration once a start time is recorded. The label reads "Running tool:", "Waiting on tool:", "Failed tool:", "Cancelled tool:", or "Used tool:", followed by the tool name. While a call runs, the duration ticks up once per second. When it completes, the duration freezes at the recorded total.

**Expanded content:** Clicking the header opens a panel that can show these sections, each only when it has content:
- **Error:** Shown only when the status is `"incomplete"` and includes an error.
- **Args:** The raw arguments text, shown when it's non-empty.
- **Approval controls:** Shown while the call requires action, followed by a receipt of the decision once it's settled.
- **Result:** Shown when a result exists. Non-string results are stringified.

**Errors, failed, and cancelled calls:** Failed and cancelled calls get their own header labels, and an error message appears in the panel only for incomplete calls that carry one. The content doesn't spell out exactly which status produces the "Failed" versus "Cancelled" label.

**Default open state:** A call opens automatically when its status is `"requires-action"`. Otherwise, it keeps whatever open or closed state the user last set. The docs don't explicitly state the initial state for other calls, though the root accepts a `defaultOpen` prop.

## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). The canvas
   frozen on 2026-10-27 (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v)
   is history, not a source. Change the token file to match, or, when the
   code's value is the one to keep, change the artifact first. Do not trust
   old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay

content.text:
You're right that it's a collapsible pattern, and our row is already halfway there. The gap is that a failed action shows no detail you can open, and today you can barely read its error at all.

**What other apps do**

- **Vercel AI Elements (Tool component):** each tool call is a collapsible row. The header has the tool name and a status badge, which reads "Error" for a failed call. Opening it shows the arguments as formatted JSON and then the error text. Their failed-call example opens on its own.
- **assistant-ui (ToolFallback):** a one-line button reading "Failed tool: <name>" with an X icon and how long it took. Clicking it opens Error, Args and Result sections, each shown only when it has content.
- **Telerik's design system and HeroUI Pro:** the same layout. The header has the name, an Error badge and a chevron; the panel holds the arguments and the error message.
- **Cursor:** when a turn finishes, its finished tool calls collapse into a "Worked for Ns" group. Our turn line copies this. Cursor's forum shows the failure side: users complain when details sit behind several toggles, and they asked for a setting to keep the request and response open.

I could not find first-party documentation for ChatGPT or Claude.ai, so I'm not claiming what they do.

**What our row does today**

The closed line reads "Worked for 4s · 1 action · 1 failed". Opening it shows one line per action, and a failed line is red and reads "Read settings · No filament preset is named …". That line is a single line cut off with an ellipsis, so in the narrow pane the error message is cut off. There is nothing else to open: no tool name, no error code, no arguments. The host also writes nothing to the app log when a call fails.

**What I propose**

- **Turn line:** unchanged, "Worked for 4s · 1 action · 1 failed ›".
- **Failed action line:** gets its own chevron and reads "Read settings · Failed". It stays closed by default, because the answer above it was fine and the red line is already the signal.
- **Details panel:** opening the failed line shows the error code (`unknown_preset`), the full message wrapped instead of cut off, the tool and server (`settings_get · jusprin-native`), and the arguments as JSON. Text is in the code font from the design tokens. A **Copy details** button copies all of it as plain text for a bug report.
- **Host:** one log line when a call fails, with the action id, tool, error code and message, so the app log has it too.
- **Tests:** Vitest tests for opening the failed line and for what Copy details copies. Then a check in the built app, with a screenshot if you approve screen control.
- **Design:** the panel is new UI, so per the design-system rules I'd add it to the turn activity board on the JusPrin v2 canvas before or alongside the code.

The bug that made this particular call fail is a separate C++ fix: `settings_get` won't read a selected preset that is hidden from the person's preset list. I left it as a proposed session card instead of folding it in.

He pointed out that the orphaned processes were the smaller problem. The bigger one was that I put that many builds there at all

2. I restarted the build three times to change its target list or to slip in a small target. Each restart cost a full set of jobs. Waiting for the running build and adding targets afterwards cost nothing.

5. Mechanism: `pkill -f "cmake --build <dir>"` kills only the wrapper. Its `ninja -C <dir>` child keeps compiling as an orphan. I never checked that a stop had worked.

**How to apply:**

- Decide the full target list once. Never restart a build to change it.
- Run one build per dir as its own process group (`set -m`, then kill with `kill -- -<pgid>`). After any stop, confirm with `pgrep -fl "ninja.*<dir>"`.
- Ask before a full-app build that the task did not require.
